items.title: 日JIC, JSR 미쓰이화학에 매각 추진
items.snippet: 일본 정부가 출자한 관민펀드 산업혁신투자기구(JIC)가 반도체 소재 기업 JSR을 미쓰이화학에 매각할 계획이다. 매각 규모는 1조3000억엔(약 11조원) 이상이다. JSR을 인수한 지 약 2년 만에 매각한다. 5일 외신에 따르면 JIC는 미쓰이화학에 JSR을 매각하는 방안을 이르면 이달 중 결정할 것으로 알려졌다. 거래가 성사되면 일본 화학업계 최대 규모 인수합병 중 하나가 될 전망이다. items.title: “핵잠-원자력협정 韓 불리해질 가능성”
items.snippet: 미국 중간선거에서 도널드 트럼프 대통령이 이끄는 공화당이 참패했지만 최근 불협화음을 겪고 있는 한미관계에 미칠 영향은 크지 않을 것이라는 관측이 나온다. 상·하원 의회 주도권을 쥐게 된 미국 민주당이 한국 등 동맹국에 대한 트럼프 행정부의 정책을 비판해 왔지만 외교 정책에 개입하는 데는 한계가 있다는 것. 오히려 이재명 정부가 추진하고 있는 전시작전통제권(전작권) 전환과 핵추진 잠수함 도입, 원자력협정 개정 등에는 걸림돌이 될 수 있다는 우려도 제기된다. 정부 안팎에서는 중간선거로 당장 한미관계에는 큰 변화가 없을 것이라는 관측이 지배적이다. 서정건 경희대 정치외교학과 교수는 “선거 패배로 트럼프 행정부의 정책 방향이 수정되고 한국에도 유리할 것이라는 기대감이 있지만 실제로는 크게 달라지지 않을 것”이라고 말했다. 다만 미 민주당이 상·하원...

items.title: 2심 “尹, 김건희와 건진 만나고도 변명 일관… 유권자 선택권 침해”
items.snippet: “당선무효나 선거비용 반환과 같은 불이익을 고려해서 형을 정할 수는 없다.” 4일 윤석열 전 대통령의 공직선거법 위반 사건 항소심을 맡은 서울고법 형사2-1부 백승엽 고법판사는 선거비용 반환은 과하다는 윤 전 대통령의 주장에 대해 이같이 설명했다. 1심 판결 이후 윤 전 대통령 측은 국민의힘이 대선 선거비용 397억 원을 반환하면 정당의 존립과 정치 활동에 중대한 영향을 미친다며 감형을 주장했다. 공직선거법에 따라 선거 범죄 등으로 벌금 100만 원 이상의 유죄 판결을 받으면 당선이 무효화되고 당시 보전받은 선거비용을 반환해야 한다. 하지만 재판부는 “엄격한 공직선거법 규정은 공정한 선거 문화를 확립하고자 하는 취지에서 국회가 도입한 것”이라며 이를 받아들이지 않았다.● “유권자 올바른 선택권 침해… 1심 판단 존중”이날 재판부는 윤 전 대통...

items.title: 397억 반환 위기 국힘 ‘사법 리스크’ 우려 커져
items.snippet: 윤석열 전 대통령이 4일 공직선거법 위반 혐의 항소심에서 1심과 같은 징역 1년 6개월과 집행유예 3년의 당선무효형을 선고받자 국민의힘에선 당혹스러운 분위기가 감지됐다. 대법원에서 형이 확정되면 2022년 대선에서 보전받은 선거비용 약 397억 원을 중앙선거관리위원회에 반환해야 하기 때문이다. 지도부는 공식 입장을 내놓진 않았지만, 추경호 대구시장의 내란 혐의 재판 1심 선고도 앞두고 있어 당내에선 ‘사법 리스크’ 우려가 다시 확산되고 있다. 국민의힘 정점식 원내대표는 이날 국회에서 기자들과 만나 윤 전 대통령의 2심 선고에 대해 “아직 대법원이 남아 있다”고만 밝혔다. 당이 사과해야 하는 것 아니냐는 질문에는 “이재명 대통령의 경우에는 대법원에서 (유죄 취지로) 파기 환송했다”면서 “민주당이 그 부분에 대해 사과한 적이 있느냐”고 반문했다....

items.title: 민주당 434억 걸린 李 선거법 재판은 당선후 중단
items.snippet: 서울고법 형사2-1부(부장판사 백승엽)는 4일 20대 대선 후보 시절 허위사실을 공표한 혐의에 대한 윤석열 전 대통령의 항소를 기각하면서 이재명 대통령의 공직선거법 위반 혐의 판결 내용을 언급했다. 이 대통령 취임 이후 중단된 재판이 퇴임 후 재개돼 벌금 100만 원 이상의 형이 확정되면 더불어민주당도 20대 대선 비용 434억 원을 국고에 반환해야 한다. 이 대통령의 공직선거법상 허위사실 공표 혐의 사건 재판은 파기환송심 재판부인 서울고법 형사7부에서 중단된 상태다. 대선 직후인 지난해 6월 당시 재판부는 헌법상 현직 대통령의 형사상 불소추 특권을 재판에도 적용해 재판을 중단시켰다. 대법원이 허위사실 공표로 판단한 이 대통령의 발언은 두 가지다. 우선 2021년 10월 국회 국정감사에서 경기 성남시 백현동 부지 용도 변경과 관련해 “국토교통...

items.title: 與, ‘조작기소 특검법’ 법사위 소위→전체회의 하루에 일방 처리
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 5일 ‘조작수사·조작기소 진상규명 특검법’(조작기소 특검법) 본회의 처리를 당론으로 채택한 지 하루 만에 국회 법제사법위원회에서 강행 처리했다. 공소취소 논란으로 6개월 넘게 계류됐던 법안을 상정해 일사천리로 밀어붙인 것. 민주당은 공소취소 조항을 삭제했지만 국민의힘은 특검 수사 대상에 이재명 대통령 사건이 포함된 점을 들어 “공소취소를 위한 빌드업”이라고 반발했다. 국민의힘이 본회의에 상정되는 모든 안건에 대한 필리버스터에 나서겠다고 밝히는 등 여야의 극단 대치 속에 산적한 민생법안은 물론 내년도 예산안 처리까지 지연될 수 있다는 우려가 나온다.● “공소취소 뺐다” vs “결국 공소취소 빌드업” 국회 법사위는 4일 오전 10시 20분경 시작된 전체회의에서 4월 발의된 조작기소 특검법을 6개월여 만에 상정했다. 민주당은 기존 법...

items.title: 김민석 ‘신천지 사과’에도, 친청 “정당법 위반 조사” 내분 격화
items.snippet: 더불어민주당 김민석 대표가 8·17 전당대회 당시 제기했던 이른바 ‘반명(반이재명)·분열주의·신천지 3자 비밀연합’ 의혹에 대해 비공개 의원총회에서 사과했지만 친청(친정청래)계가 거세게 반발하면서 사면초가에 몰린 형국이다. 조직적인 신천지 당원 가입 의혹을 덮었다는 비판에도 여권 분열 우려에 조사 결과 공개 대신 사과를 선택했지만 친청계의 역공으로 오히려 내홍이 격화하고 있는 것. 취임 100일을 20일 앞둔 김 대표는 4일 정부에 가상자산 과세 유예를 공식 제안하는 등 민생 이슈로 국면 전환을 시도했지만 조희대 대법원장 탄핵 요구 등 당내 강경파의 주장에 휘말리면서 지지율 반등이 요원한 것 아니냐는 우려도 이어지고 있다. ● 친청계, 金 면전서 “정당법 위반 조사” 김 대표는 4일 국회에서 열린 최고위원회의에서 신천지 관련 의혹에 대해 공개...

items.title: 공공재개발 띄운 李 “속도 빨라지고 부정부패 소지 줄어”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 4일 서울 주택 공급 속도전을 위한 공공재개발 사업 강화를 강조하면서 “조기에 진행될 경우에는 용적률이든 금융 지원이든 각종 인센티브를 강화하면 좋겠다”고 했다. 한국토지주택공사(LH)를 통한 공공재개발의 비중을 높이고 민간 사업의 공공 전환도 쉽게 해 주택 공급에 속도를 내겠다는 것. 이 대통령은 이날도 재차 강남 3구(강남, 서초, 송파구)의 집값이 떨어지고 있다고 강조했다.● “공공재개발 유효성… 인센티브로 사업성 높여야” 이 대통령은 이날 서울 성북구 장위동 일대를 찾아 공공재개발 현장을 시찰하고 정비사업 현장 간담회를 가졌다. 이 대통령은 “확실히 공공재개발 방식이 유효성이 있는 것 같다”며 “공공이 하면 속도도 빨라지고 부정부패 소지도 줄어든다”고 운을 뗐다. 이어 “이 정부에서 각종 인센티브를 제공하기로 했기 때문...

items.title: 李, SNS ‘X’ 이어 유튜브 ‘Y’ 신설… 靑 “소통채널 확대”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 5일 유튜브 프로그램 ‘대통령의 Y’를 시작한다고 청와대가 밝혔다. X(옛 트위터)를 활용한 소셜네트워크서비스(SNS) 소통에 이어 유튜브(Y)로 창구를 확대하겠다는 의도다. 성기홍 대통령홍보소통수석비서관은 4일 청와대에서 브리핑을 갖고 “SNS를 통한 소통 방식에서 더 나아가 유튜브를 통해서 국민의 궁금증에 답하고 정책을 설명하는 프로그램을 만들었다”며 이같이 말했다. 성 수석은 “‘Y’는 이유, 왜를 뜻하는 ‘Why’를 의미하기도 한다”며 “편안한 분위기에서 국민의 언어로 최대한 진솔하게 의견을 피력하고, 국민의 질문에 답변할 예정”이라고 말했다. 청와대는 프랭클린 루스벨트 전 미국 대통령의 노변정담(爐邊情談·따뜻한 난롯가에서 허물없이 나누는 이야기)을 참고한 것으로 알려졌다. 4일 촬영된 첫 방송은 5일 오후 9시에 공개...

items.title: 금융위, 국회 서면답변서 “집값 상승세 당분간 지속”
items.snippet: 금융당국이 국내 주택 가격 상승세가 당분간 계속될 수 있다고 전망한 것으로 4일 파악됐다. 주택담보대출 6억 원 제한 등 대출 규제에 대해선 ‘유지’ 필요성을 강조했다. 국회 정무위원회 소속 국민의힘 신동욱 의원실에 따르면 금융위는 이날 회신한 답변서에서 아파트 가격 전망에 대해 “한국은행 등에 따르면 주택 공급 부진과 그에 따른 주택가격 상승 전망 등을 감안 시 주택가격 상승세는 당분간 지속될 우려가 있다”고 답했다. 금융위는 최근 연간 수도권 아파트 착공 및 입주 물량이 10년 평균치를 밑도는 점, 5∼9월 주택가격전망지수가 ‘1년 내 상승 전망 우세’를 뜻하는 100 이상으로 유지되고 있는 점 등을 가격 상승 전망의 근거로 들었다. 다만 금융위는 “향후 주택 공급 확대, 기준금리 인상 효과 등이 가시화되면 상승세가 점차 둔화될 수 있다는...

items.title: “北해커, 이직 미끼로 바이낸스 엔지니어 낚아… 5개월간 침투 작전”
items.snippet: 북한과 연계된 해커들이 지난달 29일 세계 최대 가상자산 거래소 바이낸스에서 63억4000만 달러(약 8조4454억 원)를 탈취한 해킹을 위해 약 5개월간 치밀한 침투 작전을 벌였다고 바이낸스 측이 3일(현지 시간) 밝혔다. 이들은 가짜 채용 면접과 악성 소프트웨어 유포 등 정교한 공격 수법을 활용해 내부 시스템에 대한 접근 권한을 확보했다. 특히 바이낸스 소속 기술자의 신뢰를 얻어 내부 시스템에 침투한 뒤 가상자산 지갑 관련 핵심 업무를 담당한 다른 직원들의 접근 권한까지 탈취하는 방식으로 공격 범위를 확대했다. 바이낸스는 이날 자체 조사 보고서를 공개하며 이번 해킹을 “정교하게 설계된 다단계 공격”이라고 규정했다. 해커들이 가짜 채용 면접, 악성 소프트웨어 다운로드, 내부 인공지능(AI) 도구 활용 등 다양한 수법을 결합했다고 설명했다.●...

items.title: “공군 1호기 명단 이어 외교부 문서 2건 추가 유출”

items.title: “인천공항, 보안 검색 노동자 직고용 의무 없다”
items.snippet: 문재인 정부 ‘비정규직 제로(0) 정책’을 대표했던 인천국제공항공사(인국공)의 기존 고용 형태에 문제가 없었다는 법원 판단이 나왔다. 당시 정부는 고용 안정과 처우 개선 등을 명분으로 하청 노동자들을 공사가 직접 고용하는 정책을 추진했다. 그러나 법원은 공사의 원·하청 구조를 불법 파견이 아닌 정상적인 도급 관계로 판단했다. 하청 노동자들을 원청이 직접 고용하라는 요구가 산업계 곳곳으로 번지는 상황에서, 관련 정책의 상징이었던 인천공항공사의 직접 고용 의무를 법원이 부정한 것이다.

items.title: [Dr.이은봉의 의학 연구 다이제스트] 정신질환자, 동조편향 AI 쓰니 망상 더 깊어져
items.snippet: 정신분열증이라고 불린 조현병 환자들은 현실 인식이 떨어져 망상과 환각 증상을 보인다. 망상은 없는 것을 있다고 믿는 것이고, 환각은 없는 것이 보이거나 들리는 현상이다. 최근 대화형 인공지능 챗봇이 확산되면서, 인공지능 사용이 이런 정신병을 일으키거나 정신병을 악화시킨다는 다수의 임상 사례가 보고되고 있다. 이를 인공지능 정신병(AI psychosis)이라고 부르는데, 최근 미국 밴더빌트대 연구팀이 인공지능 정신병 발병 상황을 분석해서 미국의사협회지 정신과 편에 발표했다.

items.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
items.abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_α^{γ+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(ω^r)$ to $L^q(ω^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<r<q<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=α\in(0,1)$, and $ω\in A_{r,q}^+(γ)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_α^{γ+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. items.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
items.abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. items.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
items.abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. Each visible pulse generates photon pairs within a picosecond window...

items.title: Generative Modeling for Cascading Extremes via Autoregressive Transformers
items.abstract: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. We introduce an extremal token representation that encodes multivariate observations as a categorical sequence. A quiet token records the absence of threshold exceedances; otherwise, the token identifies the exceeding component with the largest marginal probability-scale score. The representation is invariant to componentwise strictly increasing transformations. It preserves the identity and temporal ordering of dominant exceedances but discards their magnitudes and the identities of nondominant simultaneous exceedances. A decoder-only transformer estimates the history-dependent next-token kernel on this representation, and recursive sampling generates future token sequences from the induced joint predictive law. items.title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
items.abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections,...

items.snippet: 테크윙이 메모리 시장 성장에 대응하기 위해 반도체 장비 생산능력을 확대한다. 신규 생산시설을 완전 가동하면 지난해 최대 2배에 달하는 추가 매출을 올릴 수 있을 것으로 보인다.테크윙은 약 526억원(자기자본 26.7%)을 투입해 충남 천안에 신규 공장을 세운다고 3일 공시했다. 공장 부지로 올해 확보한 천안BIT산업단지 산업시설용지를 활용한다. 공장 부지 금액은 포함되지 않았다.앞서 테크윙은 지난 3월 이사회에서 천안BIT산업단지 산업시설용지를 매입하기로 결정했다. 부지 규모는 약 3만2000평이다. 금액은 156억원이다. 부지 대

items.title: OpenAI introduces program to reduce AI data center energy demand during peak hours
items.snippet: The Grid Protectors Program applies load shedding, a technique in use since the 1970s, to data centers.

items.title: “월 500만원 번다” 유학 와서 ‘불법 배달’ 뛰는 외국인들
items.snippet: 3일 낮 12시쯤 서울 용산구 이태원의 한 샌드위치 가게에서 오토바이 헬멧을 쓴 20대 청년이 나왔다. 짙은 갈색 피부를 가진 이 청년은 손에 든 음식 봉투를 배달용 트렁크에 넣고 오토바이에 올라탔다. 본지 기자가 “한국 분이시냐”고 묻자 그는 “쏘리, 쏘리”라고 답한 뒤 오토바이를 몰고 골목으로 사라졌다. 근처에서 배달하던 이환(26)씨는 “이태원 일대나 신촌 등 서울 번화가에서는 외국인 라이더들을 자주 볼 수 있다”고 했다.

items.title: [알립니다] ‘조선 백일장’ 부울경 예선 조기 마감… 신청 서두르세요
items.snippet: 조선일보사·조선일보미디어연구소·한글학회가 주최하고 교육부가 후원하는 ‘필전 2026-조선 백일장’의 부산·울산·경남(부·울·경) 예선 신청이 조기 마감됐습니다. 당초 4일까지 신청받을 예정이었지만, 신청자가 몰리면서 일찍 마감했습니다. 부·울·경 예선은 7일 부산대에서 열립니다.

items.title: [오늘의 날씨] 2026년 11월 4일
판사들, 與에 부글부글 “전국법관 임시회의 열자”
items.snippet: 조희대 대법원장에 대한 여권의 국회 국정조사 추진과 사퇴 압박 등과 관련해 법원 내부에서 반발이 커지고 있다. 이런 상황에서 3일 전국법관대표회의를 열자는 요구가 나왔다. 남준우 서울회생법원 부장판사는 이날 법원 내부 게시판(코트넷)에 글을 올려 “전례 없는, 그리고 향후 정권과 관계없이 반복될 가능성이 농후한 대법관 재제청 사태와 관련해 전국법관대표회의 임시회의 개최를 촉구한다”고 했다.

items.title: 초대 공소청 수장에 이정현·박철우·예세민 거론
items.snippet: 법무부는 10일이나 11일 검찰총장후보추천위원회(위원장 문무일) 회의를 열고 이재명 정부의 첫 검찰총장 후보군을 추릴 것으로 3일 알려졌다. 검찰총장 후보로는 이정현(58·사법연수원 27기) 검찰총장 직무대행과 박철우(55·30기) 서울중앙지방공소청장이 유력하게 거론된다. 법조계에서는 “이재명 대통령이 기소된 사건의 ‘공소취소’ 문제에 대한 입장이 인선의 변수가 될 것”이란 관측이 나온다.

items.title: 이화영 ‘불법 대북송금’ 재심 신청
items.snippet: 쌍방울 불법 대북 송금 혐의로 기소돼 징역 7년 8개월이 확정돼 복역 중인 이화영 전 경기도 평화부지사가 3일 수원고법에 재심을 청구했다. 이 전 부지사는 대법원에서 유죄가 확정된 혐의 중 외국환거래법 위반 부분과 관련해 무죄를 인정할 증거가 발견됐다고 주장했다.

items.title: 한글 점자의 날 100주년… 손끝으로 세상을 읽다
items.snippet: ‘한글 점자의 날’을 하루 앞둔 3일 경기 수원시 팔달구 경기도시각장애인도서관에서 관계자가 점자책을 읽고 있다. 한글 점자의 날은 1926년 11월 4일 송암 박두성 선생이 한글 점자를 만들어 반포한 것을 기념하는 날이다. 올해 100주년을 맞았다.

items.title: 정부기관 이전 잇단 반발… 과천 시민들 “도시 정체성 해쳐” 시위
items.snippet: 3일 서울 종로구 정부서울청사 앞. 경기 과천 시민 250여 명이 ‘과천을 무시하는 이전 계획, 시민은 거부한다’고 쓴 손팻말을 들고 거리 행진을 벌였다. 같은 시각 청사 안에서는 행정안전부가 ‘2차 중앙행정기관 세종 이전 공청회’를 열었다.

items.title: 점점 심해지는 여학생 학폭… 소년원 가는 소녀, 4년새 2배로
items.snippet: 지난 2월 대전에 사는 A(19)양은 폭행 혐의로 소년원 6개월 송치 처분(소년보호처분 9호)을 받았다. 고등학교를 자퇴하고 ‘학교 밖 청소년’이 된 A양은 또래와 몰려다니며 금품 갈취와 폭행을 반복하다가 피해 학생 신고로 경찰에 적발됐다. 서울의 한 고교에 다니던 B(18)양은 지난 5월 중학교 동창에게 소셜미디어 메시지로 돈을 빌려달라고 요구했다가 거절당하자, 그때부터 계속 협박하고 욕설을 보냈다. B양도 결국 소년부 재판에 넘겨져 사회봉사 명령 처분(3호)을 받았다.

items.title: 중국·홍콩 대학이 ‘톱5’ 싹쓸이… 한국은 올해도 10위 내 못들어
items.snippet: 올해 ‘QS 아시아 대학 평가’에서 ‘톱 5’는 홍콩과 중국 대학이 모두 휩쓸었다. 한국 대학은 6곳이 아시아 상위 20위 안에 들었지만, 2년 연속 10위 안에 포함되지 못했다. 한국 대학의 절반 이상은 작년보다 순위가 떨어졌고, 이 추세는 수도권보다 지방 대학들에서 더 심하게 나타났다.

items.title: 겨울코트 꺼낼까 말까… “오락가락 날씨, 건조한 땅이 원인”
items.snippet: 올가을 들어 사흘 중 하루(35.5%)꼴로 전날 대비 기온 차가 5도 이상인 ‘널뛰기’ 현상을 보인 것으로 나타났다.

items.title: 한국 돌아온 ‘인도네시아 특급’… “복귀 망설일 때 남편이 응원해줘”
items.snippet: “오랜만이야. 다시 돌아온 걸 환영해!”

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [숨어있는 세계사] 2m 거대 활로… 수적 우세 佛귀족 무찌른 英평민 군대
items.snippet: 얼마 전 미 국방부는 인공지능(AI), 드론, 로봇 등 최첨단 무인 전투 체계의 실전 배치를 획기적으로 당기기 위한 국방 혁신 프로젝트를 발표했어요. 이름은 ‘프로젝트 아쟁쿠르’입니다. ‘아쟁쿠르’는 프랑스의 한 마을 이름인데요. ‘프로젝트 아쟁쿠르’는 중세 백년전쟁 중 있었던 ‘아쟁쿠르 전투’에서 따온 것이에요. 당시 영국군은 장궁(거대한 목재 활)이라는 신기술을 활용해 수적으로 우세하고 단단한 갑옷을 입은 프랑스의 정예 기병을 물리쳤어요. 아쟁쿠르 전투처럼 미 국방부는 신기술(드론·AI·로봇)을 통해 기존의 무겁고 비싼 무기체계를 압도하는 21세기 국방 혁신을 꾀하고 있어요. 오늘은 아쟁쿠르 전투에 대해 알아보도록 할게요.

items.title: ​[신문은 선생님] [예쁜 말 바른 말] [469] ‘안되다’와 ‘안 되다’
items.snippet: “공부가 잘 안돼” “그래도 공부를 포기하면 안 돼” 이 두 문장에는 ‘안돼’라는 표현이 쓰였습니다. 그런데 첫 번째 문장에서는 붙여 쓰고, 두 번째 문장에서는 띄어 썼지요. 그 이유는 무엇일까요?

items.title: 아들은 세상 속 ‘홀로서기’, 아빠는 배우로 ‘다시 서기’
items.snippet: “아들놈이 안 하던 짓을 하니까 덜컥 겁나더라고요. 엄마한테나 안기지 저한텐 무뚝뚝하거든요.”

items.title: “어머니 곁에 갈게요” 6·25학도병 ‘못 부친 편지’ 중·고교생들, 직접 기금 모아 추모비에 새겼다
items.snippet: “난 성인으로 군대를 갔는데도 힘든데, 어떻게 그 어린 나이에 나라를 지키기 위해 총을 들고 싸웠을까요.”

items.title: ‘그대 그리고 나’ 소리새 김광석 별세
items.snippet: ‘그대 그리고 나’ ‘아직도 못다한 사랑’ 등으로 1980년대 큰 인기를 끈 포크 그룹 소리새의 멤버 김광석(70)이 3일 오전 별세했다. 1981년 트리오 ‘솔개’를 결성해 트로트를 가미한 ‘아직도 못 다한 사랑’, 블루스 포크 록 ‘연극 중에서’ 등 다양한 장르를 선보였다. 1987년 ‘소리새’로 팀명을 바꾼 뒤 노래 ‘그대 그리고 나’가 큰 성공을 거뒀다. 고인의 마지막 음반 활동은 2015년 소리새의 새 멤버 윤기환과 낸 광복 70주년 기념 듀엣 음반 ‘평화의 강’(북녘땅에 보내는 노래)이다. 빈소는 교원예움 인천사랑병원, 발인은 4일 오후 1시. (032)-441-0404.

items.title: [플라자] 제주특별자치도의회 문화관광체육위원회·강봉직 의원실 ‘세계적 유산도시 실현을 위한 제주유산 정책포럼’ 개최
items.snippet: 제주특별자치도의회 문화관광체육위원회와 강봉직 의원실은 4일 오전 10시 도의회 의원회관 대회의실에서 ‘세계적 유산도시 실현을 위한 제주유산 정책포럼’을 연다.

items.snippet: ▲ 김용진 前 쌍용그룹 고문 별세, 김종호 · 김진호 · 김선영 부친상, 홍재성 JS코퍼레이션 회장 장인상=3일13시47분 삼성서울병원, 발인 5일9시, (02)3410-3151 ▲ 문철상 前 신협중앙회장 별세, 김경희 남편상, 문윤선 · 문순환 부친상, 윤연지 시부상=2일13시 전북 군산 은파장례문화원, 발인 4일9시30분, (063)472-4102

items.title: 아동문학계 원로 권오삼 시인 별세

items.title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
items.abstract: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

items.title: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
items.abstract: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. Building on this framework, we further establish a rigorous quasinormal-mode analysis that provides transparent physic...

items.title: A RISC-V Simulator for the Tenstorrent Tensix Architecture
items.abstract: RISC-V based AI accelerators have become popular and not only for AI and ML, but also as vehicles for exploring HPC workloads more generally. Tenstorrent are one example, and whilst they document their Tensix architecture in detail and develop their software stack openly, running code has historically required a physical card, and their recently released simulator targets hardware equivalence rather than introspection. In this paper we present Wolfpine, a community developed RISC-V simulator for the Tensix architecture, supporting both the Wormhole and Blackhole generations and integrating seamlessly with the TT-Metal software stack. Constructed entirely from publicly available documentation, open source software and measurements on physical hardware, Wolfpine is written in pure Python for readability and ease of modification. items.title: Effect of compensation on magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As
items.abstract: The real mechanism of ferromagnetism in III-V diluted magnetic semiconductors such as Ga$_{1-x}$Mn$_x$As is still debated. The experimental results point out the realization of appreciable ferromagnetism at filling of the impurity band close to one-half that can be expressed in terms of compensation degree. Based on our recent results on the existence of two competing mechanisms of pair indirect exchange (with ferro- and antiferro alignment of Mn $d$ shells), a theory of magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As is presented. The molecular-field-like equation is derived in which the effective exchange constant contains all necessary information about material, including the Mn content, the compensation degree, the crystal coordination, and the parameters of two competing pair exchange interactions. Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
items.abstract: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2π$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. items.title: Analytically Calibrated Upper L-Statistics for High-Dimensional Mean Change-Point Testing
items.abstract: This paper develops upper L-statistic methods for testing and localizing a high-dimensional mean change. At each candidate split, the proposed statistics rank the squared studentized CUSUM values across coordinates and aggregate either a fixed number or a fixed proportion of the largest entries. This construction connects max-type and sum-type procedures and provides sensitivity to a wide range of sparsity regimes. We establish asymptotic null distributions under an independent-component representation allowing weak cross-sectional dependence. The limiting laws are Poisson tangent processes for fixed ranks and Gaussian-process or Gumbel laws for proportional ranks. To improve finite-sample performance, we develop analytic calibrations for marginal variance estimation, cross-sectional dependence, extreme clustering, and skewness, and establish their first-order validity. items.title: Bezier-GP: Bezier-Surface-Based Gaussian Process for Chips-on-Wafer Warpage Modeling
items.abstract: As the semiconductor industry transitions to the post-Moore paradigm, wafer warpage has become a critical quality issue in advanced packaging; particularly for 3D stacking and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing where die-level deformation can affect bonding quality, interconnect reliability, and yield. However, direct high-throughput measurement of individual chip warpage remains difficult in mass-production environments, while existing wafer-level metrology systems routinely provide dense 3D shape data at the wafer scale. This paper proposes a Bezier-surface-based Gaussian Process---known as Bezier-GP---for chips-on-wafer warpage modeling. items.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$...

items.title: Polariton tweezers
items.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. items.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. items.title: Cross-Domain Joint-Embedding Pretraining For Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series
items.abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

items.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
items.abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. items.title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures

items.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. items.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
items.abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. items.abstract: Silicon Photo-Multipliers (SiPMs) are semiconductor-based photodetectors that offer performance comparable to that of traditional Photo-Multiplier Tubes (PMTs), while providing several advantages, including low operating voltage, immunity to magnetic fields, compact size, and mechanical robustness. These features have led to their widespread adoption in scintillator-based detectors for both fundamental and applied physics. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the detection of scintillation light at cryogenic temperatures in low-temperature experiments based on bolometric detectors, such as RES-NOVA and CUPID, as well as in emerging quantum applications. In the RES-NOVA experiment, radiopure PbWO$_4$ crystals are used to detect supernova neutrinos. items.title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
items.abstract: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. Although research on spatial cognition, scale, multiple representations, and systems thinking has examined aspects of this challenge, these perspectives do not always provide explicit guidance for designing learning activities that require learners to integrate information across levels. Immersive technologies offer opportunities to explore otherwise inaccessible structures, coordinate representations, and investigate system behavior, but their educational value depends on the reasoning they support. items.title: Reasoning Across Scales: Learning Challenges and Opportunities for Immersive Technologies in Chip Design Education
items.abstract: As demand for semiconductor talent grows, education must prepare learners for the complexity of modern chip design. Instruction typically relies on lectures, textbooks, software exercises, and limited laboratory experiences. Although foundational, these approaches offer limited support for understanding the spatial, multi-scale, and interconnected nature of chip design. Virtual reality (VR) can help learners visualize and interact with complex structures and processes, but its educational opportunities remain underexplored. We examined this gap through chip design curriculum analysis and semi-structured interviews with five participants representing instructional and learner perspectives. We characterized four learning demands: descriptive knowledge, procedural knowledge, relational and design-focused reasoning, and strategic decision-making. items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. items.title: Full-Potential Korringa Kohn Rostoker Study of Structural and Mechanical Properties in SiGeSn Alloys
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. The full-potential treatment also recovers the semiconducting character of Si. Further calculations for elemental Ge and Sn establish the...

items.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
items.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an addit...

items.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

items.abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. items.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. items.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
items.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. items.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. items.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
items.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

items.abstract: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. items.title: Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis: integrating reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for reliable wafer defect classification
items.abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is a complex, multi-step process that requires both high precision and low operating costs. Therefore, detecting defects in a high-volume setting is an important component of wafer map analysis for reliable production. However, most state-of-the-art deep learning approaches require a full scan of the surface, which hinders the development of high-throughput inspection systems. items.title: Cubic-Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te optical modes across the phonon and phonon-polariton regimes
items.abstract: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. Being nearly lattice-matched and moreover highly resistant to lattice and bond distortions thanks to a largely covalent bonding, cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te sets a benchmark to test the sensitivity of lattice vibrations to minimum lattice and bond distortions induced by alloying. We explore experimentally the two transverse optical regimes of cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te (x<0.7), with ab initio calculations in support: (1) the phonon-polariton regime at quasi-infinite (photon-like) wavelengths averaging over the alloy disorder, probed by forward-Raman scattering, and (2) the purely-mechanical phonon regime down to minimum wavelengths nearly matching the lattice constant zooming into the alloy disorder, achieved by inel...

items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. The stripe phases were revealed by electrical transport studies as a thermodynamic phase transition from a high temperature isotropic phase to a...

items.title: Confinement Controlled Phase-Pure 2D Layered Perovskites for Band-Edge Engineering
items.abstract: Controlling the number n of connected octahedra layers in two-dimensional metal halide perovskites enables fine control of the semiconductor band gap that is highly advantageous for optoelectronic and light emission applications. Phase purity in terms of n is crucial towards narrow emission bands and the design of band structure alignment for charge carrier funneling. We present a simple and scalable synthesis method using cesium and butylammonium as A-cations to fabricate microcrystal powders of 2D lead bromide perovskites that results in samples with very high n-phase purity. The obtained microcrystals show a sharp onset in absorbance and single narrow emission peak in UV-blue spectral range, and we confirm their structure and composition with X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy. We show that we can tailor the spectral absorption of microcrystals samples by controlled...

items.title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
items.abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. items.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
items.abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. items.abstract: Core-shell nanowires incorporating semiconductors from two groups, III-V for the core and II-VI for the shell, have been grown by molecular beam epitaxy in two dedicated chambers connected under ultra-high vacuum, and studied by electron microscopy. During the growth of the shell, the wurtzite structure of the core is replicated in the shell, without any creation of defects. This is true for a wide range of shell thickness, from about one monolayer, up to 25 nm thanks to the good lattice match between the InAs material of the core and the ZnTe material of the shell. While (1 100) m-facets and (11 20) a-facets coexist on the sidewalls of the core, during the growth of the ZnTe shell the size of the m-facets progressively increases at the expense of the a-facets which eventually disappear. items.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
items.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. items.title: Implementation and Validation of Mismatch-Tolerant High-Gain OTA with a Calibrated Negative Conductance Load
items.abstract: This paper presents the circuit-level implementation of a mismatch-tolerant high-gain operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using automatic negative-conductance calibration in 65-nm CMOS. The technique enhances OTA gain by compensating for its finite output conductance using a cross-coupled transistor pair, with an on-chip calibration loop that eliminates the need for a replica circuit or external tuning. The calibration routine increases the gain by driving the steady state error of the OTA in a unity gain feedback loop toward zero. The implementation addresses practical challenges involving comparator offset, DAC design, and subtractor gain and offset. A 6-bit capacitive DAC (CDAC)-based comparator offset calibration scheme enables reliable detection of the sub-millivolt steady state error required for high OTA gain. items.title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
items.abstract: Analog flows from specifications to a signed-off layout rarely run without manual iteration. Recent large language model (LLM) agents size circuits with optimizer loops over the device dimensions and stop at the schematic. We present OPERA (OPamp design by an Expert-taught Reasoning Agent), in which a general-purpose LLM agent designs CMOS opamps from specifications to post-layout sign-off with open-source tools. First, the designer teaches the agent the gm/ID method: map the specifications to transconductances and minimum currents, choose gm/ID per device role from characterized lookup tables, and size from equations, leaving a few knobs to search and an explainable design. Second, the agent learns the gLayout framework and taught layout practice, and writes a reusable layout generator that closes the layout and extraction loop at designer-approved gates. items.title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.title: Colossal magnetoresistance in narrow-gap magnetic semiconductor Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$
items.abstract: Discovering antiferromagnetic materials with a sizable colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) effect and precisely tuning their responses remain significant challenges in materials science. This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$. The compound undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_\mathrm{N} = 9$ K and exhibits semiconducting behavior with a low-temperature activation energy of 3.2 meV, achieving a large CMR effect of $-10^4\%$ at 9 T. Below $T_\mathrm{N}$, a distinct butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis emerges without any macroscopic ferromagnetic order, revealing a transport anomaly likely dictated by AFM domain dynamics and/or the formation and percolation of localized magnetic polarons. items.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
items.abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that lone-pair stereoactivity, not chalcogen mass, governs both properties. items.title: Numerical schemes for 1D capacitively coupled plasma fluid simulation
items.abstract: Capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) are widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, where fluid models provide an efficient approach to the simulation of the low-temperature discharge. The model considered in this work couples the electron and the ion continuity equations, the electron energy equation and the Poisson's equation for the electric potential. We investigate the numerical schemes for the simulation of the 1D-CCP. In particular, a semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is adopted for the Poisson's equation, while the remaining equations are solved using the implicit SG schemes. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to the 2D cases. Several alternative schemes are also discussed and tested. items.abstract: Nanophotonic patterning is a promising approach to enhancing light extraction in scintillator materials, with the potential to improve performance in applications such as medical imaging and particle detection. While 2D surface patterns have been successful in improving scintillator performance, the true potential of nanophotonic patterning lies in the bulk, where photons are emitted, transported, and absorbed. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the enhancement and control of scintillation using 2.5D volumetric nanophotonic patterns. Using a direct femtosecond laser writing approach, we nanofabricate square lattices of air holes into the bulk of inorganic scintillators (YAG:Ce and YAG:Yb), achieving nearly subwavelength periods compared to the peak emission wavelength and depths up to hundreds of microns, which fill a large fraction of the full thickness of the bulk. items.title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
items.abstract: Frontier large language models write correct CUDA kernels for most single-operator benchmark tasks, yet their accuracy collapses on accelerators whose architecture and programming language they have rarely seen. We present a case study of an LLM agent loop built for such accelerators. Our example is the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, programmed in a recent, sparsely documented Rust DSL, where the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days on a shared, scarce device. The loop builds its own target knowledge: it writes and checks a summary of the DSL documentation, measures the chip with microbenchmarks, records compiler-derived legality rules, and revisits this knowledge when the toolchain changes, rechecking rules and measurements where it can. A role-based search over per-kernel Design Trees explores whole-kernel designs and accumulates small accepted changes in the best version...

items.title: Converting a superseded Raith electron beam pattern generator into an unattended Critical Dimension SEM
items.abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. items.title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $μ$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. items.abstract: Phonon bursts from ionizing radiation cause correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors. We study prescribed nonequilibrium phonon pulses in a Majorana qubit formed by two $2\,μ\mathrm{m}$ proximitized nanowires. Combining the lattice Lutchyn--Oreg model, microscopic electron--phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics, we track excitation, relaxation, and logical coherence. Without quasiparticle escape, recombination restores the initial Majorana occupations in about 130 ns, while phonons exchanged during excitation and recovery can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss. For mirror-symmetric wires, the fractional coherence loss per wire is 0.75--1.0 times the excitation probability averaged over the two logical states, even at zero Majorana splitting; breaking mirror symmetry can suppress dephasing at small splitting. items.abstract: Digital SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macros enable energy-efficient CNN inference by eliminating off-chip weight transfers; however, peripheral control logic introduces three inefficiencies: bit- slice over-activation at reduced precision (L1), unnecessary accumula- tion depth (L2), and idle precision-transition stalls (L3). items.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
items.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. This cost becomes prohibitive for megapixel-scale frames with N_f~100. Although dynamic programming can reduce the computational comp...

items.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.title: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning
items.abstract: Scientific reasoning in specialized engineering fields depends on knowledge scattered across the literature, often proprietary and absent from frontier LLM training data. In such domains, frontier models tend to give generic answers. Knowledge graphs (KGs) can ground LLM reasoning. Because a graph is too large to provide in full, typical LLM+KG systems preselect a portion, deciding relevance before reasoning begins. Here we train a compact model, Prospector, to reason over a domain knowledge graph by traversing it step by step, seeking evidence in light of what it has already found. Prospector calls a small set of tools one at a time to progressively build its context, and answers with a chain of evidence that can be checked edge by edge against what its tools retrieved from the graph. items.title: ZnO/Ni interface-activated enhancement of spintronic terahertz emission from Ni/Pt bilayers
items.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ferromagnet/heavy-metal bilayers provide an efficient route for generating broadband THz radiation through ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. However, Ni/Pt bilayers usually exhibit relatively weak THz emission, limiting their use as efficient spintronic emitters. Here, we report an interface-assisted enhancement of THz emission in ZnO/Ni/Pt heterostructures. By placing ZnO underneath Ni while preserving the direct Ni/Pt contact, the THz amplitude is increased by up to approximately 2.8 times compared with the Ni/Pt reference. The enhanced emission reverses polarity with the magnetic field and follows the expected angular dependence of ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin--photon interfaces for scalable quantum networks require bright optical transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent spin control. Donor spins in direct-bandgap semiconductors combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate coherent optical control of a single Cl donor electron spin in ZnSe. Resonant excitation reveals spin relaxation dynamics and measures spin coherence through coherent population trapping (CPT). Off-resonant ultrafast pulses are implemented to drive spin Rabi oscillations and demonstrate Ramsey interference. Multiple dark resonances in the CPT spectrum further reveal hyperfine coupling between the electron and the I=3/2 Cl nucleus. Together, these results demonstrate the first c...

items.title: Bringing Hardware Security Education to All: A Seamless Curriculum Integration Approach
items.abstract: Cybersecurity education has predominantly focused on software and network security, under the assumption that the underlying hardware is trustworthy. Threats introduced through the global semiconductor supply chain, together with vulnerabilities arising during design and integration, challenge the assumption that hardware can serve as an unquestioned root of trust. Sensor-enabled systems and machine-learning accelerators further expand the hardware attack surface. The undergraduate curriculum of electrical and computer engineering and computer science programs has not evolved accordingly. Core courses cover the design and the functionality of hardware while the security aspects remain overlooked, and dedicated hardware security (HS) courses are elective, scarce, and often restricted to graduate students. items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalize...

items.title: Residual AM and PM Noise of Selected X-Band Amplifiers
items.abstract: In microwave systems design, amplitude modulation (AM) noise is often ignored relative to phase modulation (PM) noise. However, in high-performance applications requiring ultra-low PM noise, AM noise becomes a critical limiting factor due to AM-to-PM conversion mechanisms. Because AM noise specifications are rarely, if ever, provided for commercial microwave components, this study characterizes the residual AM and PM noise of several 10 GHz amplifiers. We present performance data for various Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) amplifier designs and demonstrate the noise reduction achieved through power-summed configurations. For example, a discrete-die GaAs HBT amplifier achieves residual PM noise below $-160$ dBrad$^2$/Hz and AM noise of approximately $-155$ dB/Hz at a 1 kHz offset in a quad power-summed configuration. A notable finding is that the majority of amplifier designs surv...

items.title: Passive-reflector bounds and robust bilateral nonequilibrium Casimir repulsion
items.abstract: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations can generate repulsive Casimir--Lifshitz pressures, but optimizing a cavity at one operating point does not establish that the repulsion survives uncertainty or exceeds ordinary far-field radiation pressure. We formulate a two-sided biased-semiconductor cavity as a constrained max--min problem that maximizes the smaller outward pressure on its two reflectors. In the optically thick-slab limit, identical reflectors admit a symmetric global optimizer, and a passive-reflector bound separates cavity enhancement from the driven far-field plateau. At $300~\mathrm{K}$, a biased-GaAs cavity with $\pm10~\mathrm{nm}$ gap uncertainty and $\pm0.005$ drive uncertainty sustains a worst-case pressure of $2.257~\mathrm{mPa}$ with ideal reflectors. Reoptimization with a causal gold response retains $2.164~\mathrm{mPa}$. The nominal and robust optima lie within...

items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: We develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) to evaluate electronic observables without explicitly constructing occupied eigenstates. Nested Fourier probes progressively cancel nearby cross terms, while exponential or algebraic density-matrix decay suppresses distant contributions. Refinement reuses all previous matrix-function responses to evaluate diverse electronic observables. Electron density and nonlocal forces illustrate diagonal extraction and off-diagonal contraction, respectively. A locality-based decay model fitted to changes across completed levels estimates residual errors from the unresolved pairs without additional matrix-function applications. Tests using fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians for semiconductors, metals, and thermally perturbed silica cover different decay ranges and periodic cell geometries. About 90% of the assessed density and nonlocal force prediction...

items.title: Laser-Induced Rashba Spin-Orbit Torques in Multiferroic Semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te
items.abstract: The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and carrier-mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge0.85Mn0.15Te using time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser-induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin-orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser-induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba split, spin-locked valence band states and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. The transient change in magnetic properties, observed as variations in the amp...

items.title: Uncertainty and Business-Aware Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Semiconductor Manufacturing
items.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimates guide maintenance in semiconductor manufacturing, where a late intervention can disrupt production but an early one discards usable equipment life. A single prediction does not express the uncertainty needed to choose between these outcomes. We combine Deep Learning (DL) sequence models with Simoultaneous Quantile Regression (SQR) to estimate RUL at selectable quantile levels, and evaluate maintenance decisions using Unexpected Breaks (UB), Unexploited Lifetime (UL), and a cost-weighted objective. On the $F_1$ fault mode of the 2018 PHM Data Challenge (PHM18) ion-milling dataset, we compare recurrent, Transformer, and State Space Models (SSM) architectures. Diagonal State Spaced (S4D) gives the strongest overall RUL accuracy across the evaluated quantiles. Varying the quantile and maintenance window exposes the trade-off between failure risk and earl...

items.title: A swept-source dual-comb spectrometer on a chip
items.abstract: Dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) enables high-speed, high-resolution spectroscopy by down-converting optical spectra to the radio-frequency (RF) domain through the interference of two mutually detuned frequency combs. Accurately resolving narrow molecular absorption features requires closely spaced comb lines generated by large laser cavities with long round-trip times, thereby hindering the miniaturization of high-resolution spectrometers. Here, we circumvent this limitation by demonstrating a swept-source dual-comb spectrometer using two unidirectional racetrack semiconductor lasers integrated on the same chip. The traveling-wave frequency combs are generated by strong RF injection at the laser cavity round-trip frequency of 14.3~GHz---otherwise known as quantum walk combs---and are continuously tuned in frequency by varying the laser drive currents. This enables continuous spectral sampli...

items.title: DACRI: Decision-Aware Causal Intervention Ranking for Critical Supply Chains
items.abstract: Detecting or attributing a supply-chain disruption is not the same as selecting the intervention that maximizes recoverable net value. We present CriticalSCM-Bench v1, a controlled synthetic benchmark with causal ground truth, paired factual/counterfactual rollouts, and an explicit net-value objective. Relative to a full-information train-selected static benchmark, LambdaMART improves median normalized net value by 5.7--16.2\%, with paired statistical support on the semiconductor and critical-material archetypes but not on digital infrastructure. On digital infrastructure, a domain-informed constant-buffer policy remains stronger, showing that greater model complexity is not uniformly justified. Across partial and delayed settings, LambdaMART retains 33--75\% of full-clamp value. Stress tests further show that intervention fidelity, timing, cost, and held-out disruptions can alter policy...

items.title: Fluctuation electrodynamics of quantum capacitance in electron bilayers
items.abstract: Capacitance provides a thermodynamic probe of interacting electrons. It characterizes the energy cost of transferring charge between conductors, which, in low-dimensional systems, is governed by exchange and correlation effects in addition to electrostatic contributions. We develop a theory of the quantum capacitance of electron double layers, semiconductor quantum wells as well as monolayer and bilayer graphene devices, focusing on the contribution generated by interlayer correlations. Within a functional-integral formulation we show that the separation-dependent part of the ground-state energy is, at the level of ring diagrams, exactly the nonretarded Lifshitz expression for the van der Waals energy of two conducting sheets, with reflection amplitudes built from the layer polarizabilities. The interlayer correction to the inverse capacitance is the second density derivative of this ene...

items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are conne...

items.title: Controllable Quantum Spin Hall Phases in Bi$_2$Te$_3$-Family van der Waals Heterobilayers
items.abstract: The tunability and control of topological edge/surface states are crucial for the development of new device applications. In this work, by combining first-principles calculations and Wannier-based tight-binding methods, we show the emergence of quantum spin Hall phases in van der Waals heterostructures formed by stacking two trivial quintuple layers from the Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family. We demonstrate the tunability of the edge states under interlayer strain and external electric field effects, suggesting the possibility of switching topological edge states on/off by external control. Additionally, the quantum spin Hall edge channels remain robust against interlayer twist, highlighting their stability against external perturbations. Our results provide a new way to create and manipulate two-dimensional topological phases in systems based on Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family, which can be valuable for practica...

items.title: Dispersive mode coupling in $p$-doped semiconductor nanomechanical resonators
items.abstract: Dispersive coupling between vibrational modes with different frequencies is a major nonlinear dynamical effect. We show that in $p$-doped semiconductors such coupling is strongly enhanced. Moreover, the coupling parameters increase with the order of the nonlinearity. The doping-induced dispersive coupling becomes much stronger than the intrinsic one already for moderately strong doping. Its dependence on the hole density is nonmonotonic, and the temperature dependence becomes nonmonotonic for higher densities. Relevant mesoscopic frequency fluctuations are briefly discussed. The results are applied to Si resonators, where doping is used to compensate the temperature dependence of a clock mode, whereas another low-frequency mode is used as a thermometer to enable temperature stabilization.
